section_summary: This section comprises internal transmission lists maintained by the American Embassy in Tokyo recording despatches and telegrams sent to the Department of State during December 1938. Pages 433–436 continue a register of Embassy despatches (Nos. 3534–3590), while pages 437–438 list telegrams sent during the month (Nos. 759–781 and 801–819). The logged communications detail Japanese military operations and political policy announcements in China, British and American diplomatic representations regarding property damage and navigation rights, and administrative operations of the Tokyo Embassy.

subfiles.about: Register of diplomatic despatches Nos. 3534 through 3590 sent from the American Embassy in Tokyo to the Department of State between December 22 and December 31, 1938.
subfiles.summary: This four-page document continues an ongoing register of numbered despatches forwarded by the American Embassy in Tokyo to the Department of State in late December 1938. Entries index communications regarding Japanese policy pronouncements in China, the Imperial Conference, the establishment of the Asia Promotion Board (Kōa-in), and diplomatic discussions between Foreign Minister Hachirō Arita and ambassadors Joseph Grew and Sir Robert Craigie. The list documents extensive American and British representations concerning war damage to mission and business properties in China, aerial bombings, Yangtze navigation restrictions, and Chinese government railway obligations. Administrative items such as embassy repairs, diplomatic visa reports, and language study examinations are also catalogued.
subfiles.title: List of Despatches Sent to the Department of State (Nos. 3534–3590)

subfiles.about: Index of telegrams Nos. 759 through 819 sent by the American Embassy in Tokyo to the Department of State during December 1938.
subfiles.summary: This two-page transmission list catalogues telegrams sent by the Tokyo Embassy to Washington in December 1938, covering telegrams Nos. 759–781 (December 1–14) and Nos. 801–819 (December 23–31). The telegrams summarize urgent diplomatic developments, notably high-level conferences between Foreign Minister Arita, Ambassador Grew, and Ambassador Craigie regarding Anglo-American policy toward Japan's new order in East Asia. Other indexed messages address Japanese gold exports, bombings of American mission compounds (including the Nyhus casualty incident at Tungpeh), the Turevic narcotics investigation, and routine embassy management including code books and staffing requisitions.
subfiles.title: Telegrams Sent to the Department During December 1938
